4) In a classification model, the proportion of benefit to harm ratio will be more predictive of whether someone chooses an experimental treatment than the benefits or risks alone. 


```{r}
data <- read.csv("../data/Cleaned_Pilot/Cleaned_Pilot.09.csv", header=TRUE, comment.char="#", stringsAsFactors=TRUE) %>% 
    dplyr::select(user_id, risk, gain, ratio, experimental_treatment_selected, trial_index, Yes, No) %>% filter(Yes > 10 & No  > 10)
#use subjects with at least 10 observations for each class of the DV
```


```{r}
#data structures to hold results
risk<- list()
gain<- list() #predictions for risk gain model
ratio<- list() #predictions for ratio model

z <- list() 
y <- list()
x <- list()
subject.accuracy.RiskGain <- list()
subject.accuracy.Ratio <- list()

for (s in data$user_id){
sub = filter(data, user_id == s)

all_trials <-unique(sub[['trial_index']])
scale <- c("risk", "gain")

sub[,scale] <- scale(sub[,scale])  

set.seed(1)
#we create cross validation folds using caret's createFolds
num_folds <- 10
folds<-createFolds(all_trials,k=num_folds,list=TRUE,returnTrain=TRUE)

    #we create cross validation folds using caret's createFolds
    for(i in 1:num_folds){
      train_ids<- folds[[i]]
      test_ids<-all_trials[!all_trials%in%folds[[i]]]
       #generate train/test
      train<-subset(sub,trial_index%in%train_ids)
      test<-subset(sub,trial_index%in%test_ids)
  
      #fit models
      m.risk.gain <- glm(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain, data = train, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
      m.ratio <- glm(experimental_treatment_selected ~ ratio, data = train, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  
      test_trials <- unique(test[['trial_index']])
      prediction_subset <- subset(test,trial_index==test_trials)
    
       #test predictions
       y_pred.rg <- predict(m.risk.gain,prediction_subset, type="response")
       y_pred.r <- predict(m.ratio,prediction_subset, type="response")

       #test results for each fold of each model in confusion matrixes
       risk.gain[[i]]  <-  table(ifelse(y_pred.rg >.50,"Yes to treatment","No to treatment"),prediction_subset$experimental_treatment_selected)
       ratio[[i]]  <-  table(ifelse(y_pred.r >.50,"Yes to treatment","No to treatment"),prediction_subset$experimental_treatment_selected)
       }
      #calcuate subject level prediction accuracy for each fold
     for (ii in 1:10){
      #risk gain model
      n <- sum(risk.gain[[ii]]) # number of instances
      diag <- diag(risk.gain[[ii]]) 
      z[ii] <- sum(diag) / n # Calculate the Accuracy
      #ratio model
      n <- sum(ratio[[ii]]) # number of instances
      diag <- diag(ratio[[ii]]) 
      y[ii] <- sum(diag) / n # Calculate the Accuracy
      }
  #bring the lists for each fold into a df for each model by subject
  sub.accuracy.1 = do.call(rbind, z)
  sub.accuracy.2 = do.call(rbind, y)
  #calulate the average prediction accuracy for each subject 
  subject.accuracy.RiskGain[[s]] = apply(sub.accuracy.1, 2, function(x) mean(x))
  subject.accuracy.Ratio[[s]] = apply(sub.accuracy.2, 2, function(x) mean(x))
}

subject.accuracy.rg.df = do.call(rbind, subject.accuracy.RiskGain)
subject.accuracy.r.df = do.call(rbind, subject.accuracy.Ratio)

accuracy <- cbind(subject.accuracy.rg.df,subject.accuracy.r.df)
colnames(accuracy) = c('RiskGain', 'Ratio') 






########
results <-  melt(accuracy,
                     variable.name = "Model", 
                       value.name = "Accuracy")
colnames(results) = c('subject', 'Model', 'Accuracy') 
results$subject <- as.factor(results$subject)


results[order(results$Model, results$subject), ]

t.test(Accuracy ~ Model, results)


ggplot(results, aes(Model, Accuracy, fill=Model)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_boot, geom = "pointrange") + 
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "red")
```


```{r}
#data structures to hold results
risk<- list()
gain<- list() #predictions for risk gain model
ratio<- list() #predictions for ratio model

z <- list() 
y <- list()
x <- list()
subject.accuracy.Risk <- list()
subject.accuracy.Gain <- list()
subject.accuracy.Ratio <- list()

for (s in data$user_id){
sub = filter(data, user_id == s)

all_trials <-unique(sub[['trial_index']])

set.seed(12)
#we create cross validation folds using caret's createFolds
num_folds <- 10
folds<-createFolds(all_trials,k=num_folds,list=TRUE,returnTrain=TRUE)

    #we create cross validation folds using caret's createFolds
    for(i in 1:num_folds){
      train_ids<- folds[[i]]
      test_ids<-all_trials[!all_trials%in%folds[[i]]]
       #generate train/test
      train<-subset(sub,trial_index%in%train_ids)
      test<-subset(sub,trial_index%in%test_ids)
  
      #fit models
      m.risk <- glm(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk, data = train, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
      m.gain <- glm(experimental_treatment_selected ~ gain, data = train, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
      m.ratio <- glm(experimental_treatment_selected ~ ratio, data = train, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  
      test_trials <- unique(test[['trial_index']])
      prediction_subset <- subset(test,trial_index==test_trials)
    
       #test predictions
       y_pred.risk <- predict(m.risk,prediction_subset, type="response")
       y_pred.gain <- predict(m.gain,prediction_subset, type="response")
       y_pred.ratio <- predict(m.ratio,prediction_subset, type="response")

       #test results for each fold of each model in confusion matrixes
       risk[[i]]  <-  table(ifelse(y_pred.risk >.50,"Yes to treatment","No to treatment"),prediction_subset$experimental_treatment_selected)
       gain[[i]]  <-  table(ifelse(y_pred.gain >.50,"Yes to treatment","No to treatment"),prediction_subset$experimental_treatment_selected)
       ratio[[i]]  <-  table(ifelse(y_pred.ratio >.50,"Yes to treatment","No to treatment"),prediction_subset$experimental_treatment_selected)
       }
      #calcuate subject level prediction accuracy for each fold
     for (ii in 1:10){
      #risk  model
      n <- sum(risk[[ii]]) # number of instances
      diag <- diag(risk[[ii]]) 
      x[ii] <- sum(diag) / n # Calculate the Accuracy
      # gain model
      n <- sum(gain[[ii]]) # number of instances
      diag <- diag(gain[[ii]]) 
      y[ii] <- sum(diag) / n # Calculate the Accuracy
      #ratio model
      n <- sum(ratio[[ii]]) # number of instances
      diag <- diag(ratio[[ii]]) 
      z[ii] <- sum(diag) / n # Calculate the Accuracy
      }
  #bring the lists for each fold into a df for each model by subject
  sub.accuracy.1 = do.call(rbind, x)
  sub.accuracy.2 = do.call(rbind, y)
  sub.accuracy.3 = do.call(rbind, z)

  #calulate the average prediction accuracy for each subject 
  subject.accuracy.Risk[[s]] = apply(sub.accuracy.1, 2, function(x) mean(x))
  subject.accuracy.Gain[[s]] = apply(sub.accuracy.2, 2, function(x) mean(x))
  subject.accuracy.Ratio[[s]] = apply(sub.accuracy.3, 2, function(x) mean(x))
}

subject.accuracy.r.df = do.call(rbind, subject.accuracy.Risk)
subject.accuracy.g.df = do.call(rbind, subject.accuracy.Gain)
subject.accuracy.ra.df = do.call(rbind, subject.accuracy.Ratio)

accuracy <- cbind(subject.accuracy.r.df,subject.accuracy.g.df, subject.accuracy.ra.df)
colnames(accuracy) = c('Risk','Gain','Ratio') 

```
